## Verdict

Not usable as-is. Two short sentences, and both carry substantiation risk; neither gives hospital procurement anything to evaluate.

## The problems

**"Surgeons love it" — unsubstantiated third-party endorsement.**
A collective satisfaction claim with no source, no n, no method. German health-sector advertising applies a strict standard (*Strengeprinzip*): the advertiser bears the burden of proving the claim's accuracy, and vague collective endorsements don't survive it. Hooks: UWG §5, HWG §3. If the copy also sits on a publicly accessible website — which most procurement-facing content does — it is simultaneously lay-facing, and HWG §11 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 (Gutachten/Zeugnisse) and Nr. 11 (Äußerungen Dritter) come into play. HWG §6 sets the fix: name the author, the date, and quote accurately.

**"actually enjoy using" — implicit comparative advertising.**
"Actually" only works by implying the competition is unpleasant. That's an implied comparison against unnamed competitors, and UWG §6 Abs. 2 permits comparison only on objective, verifiable, relevant characteristics. "Enjoy" is none of those. This is classic *Abmahnung* material for a competitor or the Wettbewerbszentrale.

**Handling is a performance attribute here.**
For a manual retractor, ergonomics *is* the performance story — so "enjoy using" isn't purely emotional puffery, it brushes MDR Art. 7 (no claims ascribing properties the device doesn't have). The good news: you almost certainly already have the evidence. Your IEC 62366-1 usability engineering file, plus any grip-force or fatigue data, converts the vibe into a defensible claim.

**Register is wrong for the audience.**
Hospital procurement in Germany buys on reprocessing validity, unit cost over lifecycle, and variant coverage. This copy is consumer-voiced and names neither the product nor the manufacturer.

**Language.** German market, German copy. Advertising isn't legally required to be in German, but English consumer-voiced copy to a German *Einkaufsabteilung* costs you credibility for no gain.

## One thing to check on your side

"Class I reusable" for a retractor means **Class Ir** — MDR Art. 2(9) lists "retracting" explicitly in the reusable-surgical-instrument definition. That triggers notified body involvement for reprocessing aspects (Art. 52(7)(c)), so your CE mark carries a four-digit NB number. Procurement will look for it. If your artwork shows a bare CE mark, that's a bigger problem than the copy.

## Suggested rewrite

```
[Produktname] — Wundspreizer für die offene Chirurgie

Zur manuellen Retraktion von Gewebe und Freihaltung des
Operationssitus bei offenen Eingriffen.

· Ergonomisch geformter Griff, ausgelegt für ermüdungsarmes
  Halten bei langen Eingriffen
· Edelstahl [1.4021], validiert für [n] Aufbereitungszyklen
  nach ISO 17664
· Dampfsterilisation 134 °C / [x] min
· [n] Blattgrößen / Varianten

CE [NB-Nr.] · Basic UDI-DI: [...] · Hersteller: [...]
```

Two notes on that draft: the ergonomics bullet is only sayable if your usability file or grip-force data supports it — otherwise cut to a neutral description of the handle geometry. And if you want to keep the endorsement angle, it needs to look like this:

> In einer Anwenderbefragung ([Institut], [MM/JJJJ], n = [x] Chirurginnen und Chirurgen) bewerteten [x] % die Griffergonomie mit „gut" oder „sehr gut".

Same persuasive work, sourced per HWG §6, and it survives an *Abmahnung*.

## Verdict

Not usable as written. Two sentences, three substantiation problems, and a tone that works against a procurement audience. Nothing here is *irreparably* non-compliant — the claims are just unsupported and unanchored, which is fixable.

## Findings

**1. "Surgeons love it" — unsubstantiated empirical claim**

It reads as a factual assertion about user sentiment, so it needs evidence on file: a user survey, post-market clinical follow-up satisfaction data, or usability/formative study results with N, population, method, and date. Without that it's misleading under UWG § 5 and MDR Art. 7(1) (claims in advertising must not mislead).

Useful nuance: HWG § 11 (the testimonial/endorsement restrictions) applies only to advertising **outside** professional circles, so a properly attributed professional testimonial *is* available to you here in a way it wouldn't be in patient-facing copy. But HWG § 6 still wants the author, date, and content stated when you advertise with expert statements — so "surgeons" as an anonymous collective is the worst of both worlds: it carries testimonial weight with none of the attribution that would make it defensible.

**2. "actually enjoy using" — implicit disparaging comparison**

"Actually" only works by implying competitor retractors are unpleasant to use. That's comparative advertising under UWG § 6 without naming a comparator, which means it fails § 6(2) on two counts: the comparison isn't on objectively verifiable, relevant criteria, and it denigrates unnamed competitors' products. Delete the word, or convert it into a real comparison you can defend on a measurable attribute (grip force, mass, hand fatigue scores).

**3. No anchor to intended purpose**

The intended purpose is "manual retraction of tissue to maintain surgical site exposure during open procedures." Neither sentence connects to it. MDR Art. 7(1)(d) prohibits suggesting uses beyond the intended purpose — you're not doing that, so this isn't a violation, but it's a missed requirement of a different kind: a procurement reviewer can't map "enjoy" to any tender award criterion.

**4. Class Ir, not plain Class I**

A reusable surgical retractor is class **Ir** under MDR, meaning notified body involvement covering reprocessing, cleaning, disinfection, sterilisation, maintenance and the related IFU sections. Flagging this because it constrains the copy you're likely to write next: any claim about autoclave cycles, service life, number of validated reprocessings, or "maintenance-free" must match the NB-assessed reprocessing validation exactly. Don't let marketing round those numbers up.

**5. Channel and language**

Copy is in English for a German market and a Fachkreise audience. Advertising language isn't itself mandated (unlike the IFU, which must be German), but English copy to hospital procurement is a self-inflicted wound. Separately: the Fachkreise classification only holds if the channel is genuinely gated. An open website or general-readership trade press pulls you back under the stricter Publikumswerbung rules, including HWG § 11.

## Suggested rewrites

These assume you hold the supporting data; each needs a substantiation file entry.

> **Retraktor [Name] — für konstante Situsexposition bei offenen Eingriffen.**
> Ergonomischer Griff, [X] g, [n] validierte Aufbereitungszyklen gemäß Gebrauchsanweisung. Verfügbar in [n] Blattgrößen.

> **Konstante Exposition, geringere Handermüdung.**
> In einer Usability-Studie mit [n] Chirurg:innen ([Jahr]) bewerteten [x] % die Handhabung mit [Ergebnis]. [Quelle]

> **Weniger Nachjustieren, planbare Aufbereitungskosten.**
> [n] Aufbereitungszyklen validiert · [Material] · [Normbezug] · Katalog-Nr. [xxx]

Procurement buys on objective criteria — reprocessing cost per cycle, instrument set compatibility, sizes, material, standards conformity, delivery terms. Lead with those and the ergonomics claim becomes credible support rather than the whole pitch.

## Before publication

- [ ] Written substantiation for every claim, dated, with method and source — retained and retrievable
- [ ] CE marking complete and Ir notified body certificate in force before any promotion
- [ ] Claims cross-checked against IFU and technical documentation for consistency
- [ ] Ergonomics/satisfaction claims traced to a specific study, not to sales anecdote
- [ ] Channel gating confirmed if you rely on Fachkreise status
- [ ] Final German wording reviewed by counsel — I've flagged the framework (MDR Art. 7, UWG §§ 5, 5a, 6, HWG §§ 6 and 11, MPDG), but HWG's scope for medical devices was narrowed by the 2021 MDR adaptation legislation and the exact section applicability is worth confirming rather than taking from me.
